page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running on an Intel Xeon processor with a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance includes 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, and features 45 MB of L3 cache. It contains no bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Hardware instruction support includes standard AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA flags, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

In performance evaluations, the n1-standard-8 demonstrates baseline x86_64 compute capabilities. CPU benchmarks via stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark reflect legacy-tier performance, including a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and multi-core score of 3531.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 45.37 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in average benchmark tiers. Workload metrics show 5.27 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 4.56 GB/sec. Small LLM text generation using a 135M model delivers 100.1 tokens per second.

The hardware configuration provides balanced compute and memory capacity for standard workloads. Lower single-core performance compared to newer CPU generations represents a main architectural tradeoff. The instance is appropriate for general microservices, light web serving, development environments, and background data processing tasks.
